title: Song of Solomon Chapter 1 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Song of Solomon chapter 1 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Song of Solomon Chapter 1 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Song of Solomon Chapter 1.

questions.question: What is the title given to the song in Song of Solomon 1:1?
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:1 states, 'The song of songs, which is Solomon's.'

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 1:2, what is better than wine?
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:2 says, 'for thy love is better than wine.'

questions.question: Why do the virgins love the one spoken of in Song of Solomon 1:3?
options: Because of the savour of his good ointments
questions.correctAnswer: Because of the savour of his good ointments
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:3 explains, 'Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee.'

questions.question: What does the speaker ask to be done in Song of Solomon 1:4?
options: Draw me, we will run after thee
questions.correctAnswer: Draw me, we will run after thee
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:4 states, 'Draw me, we will run after thee: the king hath brought me into his chambers...'

questions.question: How does the speaker describe herself in Song of Solomon 1:5?
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:5 says, 'I am black, but comely, O ye daughters of Jerusalem.'

questions.question: Why does the speaker say not to look upon her in Song of Solomon 1:6?
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:6 states, 'Look not upon me, because I am black, because the sun hath looked upon me.'

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 1:6, who made the speaker keeper of the vineyards?
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:6 says, 'my mother's children were angry with me; they made me the keeper of the vineyards.'

questions.question: True or False: Song of Solomon 1:1 states the song belongs to David.
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:1 clearly states the song is Solomon's, not David's.

questions.question: True or False: Song of Solomon 1:2 mentions kisses from the mouth.
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:2 says, 'Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth.'

questions.question: True or False: Song of Solomon 1:5 compares the speaker to the curtains of Solomon.
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:5 states, 'I am black, but comely... as the curtains of Solomon.'

questions.question: True or False: Song of Solomon 1:6 says the speaker kept her own vineyard.
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:6 says, 'but mine own vineyard have I not kept.'

questions.question: In Song of Solomon 1, which event happens first?
options: The king brings the speaker into his chambers
The speaker declares she is black but comely
The speaker laments not keeping her vineyard
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:2 has the speaker asking for kisses before the king brings her into his chambers in 1:4 and the self-description in 1:5-6.

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 1:3, what is compared to ointment poured forth?
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:3 states, 'thy name is as ointment poured forth.'

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 1:4, who loves the speaker?
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:4 ends with, 'the upright love thee.'

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 1:5, to what are the daughters of Jerusalem compared?
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:5 says, 'O ye daughters of Jerusalem, as the tents of Kedar.'

medium.title: Song of Solomon Chapter 1 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Song of Solomon Chapter 1 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 1:7, what is the speaker asking about the one whom her soul loves?
options: Where he feeds and makes his flock rest at noon
Where he keeps his vineyard and olives
What kind of weapons he carries
questions.correctAnswer: Where he feeds and makes his flock rest at noon
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:7 asks, 'Tell me... where thou feedest, where thou makest thy flock to rest at noon,' showing the speaker's desire to know the beloved's daily care and rest places.

questions.question: In Song of Solomon 1:8, what advice is given if the beloved does not know where to feed the flock?
options: Go forth by the footsteps of the flock and feed the kids beside the shepherds' tents
Wait patiently until the flock returns
Seek help from the elders of the city
questions.correctAnswer: Go forth by the footsteps of the flock and feed the kids beside the shepherds' tents
questions.explanation: Verse 8 advises, 'If thou know not... go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds' tents,' instructing to follow the path and care for the young sheep near the shepherds.

questions.question: How does Song of Solomon 1:9 metaphorically describe the beloved?
options: As a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots
As a lion roaring in the forest
As a mighty cedar in Lebanon
As a swift eagle in the sky
questions.correctAnswer: As a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots
questions.explanation: Verse 9 states, 'I have compared thee... to a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots,' using the imagery of powerful horses in royal chariots to illustrate strength and beauty.

questions.question: What adornments are mentioned in Song of Solomon 1:10 as decorating the beloved's cheeks and neck?
options: Rows of jewels on cheeks, chains of gold on neck
Garlands of flowers and bronze chains
questions.correctAnswer: Rows of jewels on cheeks, chains of gold on neck
questions.explanation: Verse 10 describes, 'Thy cheeks are comely with rows of jewels, thy neck with chains of gold,' highlighting the beloved's exquisite beauty and adornment.

questions.question: What is promised in Song of Solomon 1:11 regarding the beloved's borders?
options: Borders of gold with studs of silver will be made
Borders of embroidered cloth will be sewn
Borders of precious stones will be arranged
Borders of iron will be fashioned
questions.correctAnswer: Borders of gold with studs of silver will be made
questions.explanation: Verse 11 says, 'We will make thee borders of gold with studs of silver,' expressing a promise of honorable and precious decoration.

questions.question: What does Song of Solomon 1:12 say about the spikenard while the king sits at his table?
options: It is offered as a gift
questions.explanation: Verse 12 states, 'While the king sitteth at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof,' indicating the fragrance fills the surroundings during the king's presence.

questions.question: How do Song of Solomon 1:7 and 1:8 together teach about seeking guidance in uncertain times?
options: If one does not know where to go, following the path of others and seeking support is advised
One should stay isolated and avoid company
Ignoring the problem will make it go away
One must rely solely on their own strength without guidance
questions.correctAnswer: If one does not know where to go, following the path of others and seeking support is advised
questions.explanation: Verse 7 expresses uncertainty about where the beloved feeds his flock, and verse 8 advises to follow the footsteps of the flock and feed beside the shepherds, teaching that seeking guidance and community support is wise in uncertainty.

questions.question: Based on Song of Solomon 1:9-10, what biblical virtue can be drawn from the description of the beloved's beauty and strength?
options: Appreciation for God-given gifts and honoring others
Pride in one's own achievements without humility
questions.correctAnswer: Appreciation for God-given gifts and honoring others
questions.explanation: Verses 9-10 use imagery of majestic horses and precious jewels, encouraging believers to value and honor the gifts God provides in others rather than envy or pride.

questions.question: What does Song of Solomon 1:12 teach about living faithfully in the presence of authority or leadership?
options: Faithfulness and devotion can be a fragrant offering even in everyday moments
One should hide their true self to please leaders
Obedience is only necessary in public
Leaders do not notice small acts of faith
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness and devotion can be a fragrant offering even in everyday moments
questions.explanation: Verse 12 depicts the spikenard's fragrance sent forth while the king sits at his table, symbolizing that devotion and faith can be pleasing and noticeable even in ordinary, daily circumstances.

questions.question: How does Song of Solomon 1:7-8 illustrate the importance of community and fellowship in spiritual growth?
options: By encouraging following the flock’s footsteps and feeding beside shepherds’ tents when unsure
By promoting isolation to avoid distractions
By suggesting self-reliance without others’ help
By advising competition among the flock members
questions.correctAnswer: By encouraging following the flock’s footsteps and feeding beside shepherds’ tents when unsure
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 highlight that when uncertain, one should seek the community path and fellowship (shepherds’ tents), teaching the value of shared guidance and support in spiritual journey.

questions.question: What practical lesson about generosity and honor is found in Song of Solomon 1:11?
options: We should generously adorn and honor those we love
We must keep all gifts for ourselves
We should only give when asked
Honor is shown only through words, not actions
questions.correctAnswer: We should generously adorn and honor those we love
questions.explanation: Verse 11's promise to make borders of gold with studs of silver symbolizes the biblical principle of honoring others with generosity and meaningful gifts.

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 1:7, what does the speaker imply by asking why she should be 'as one that turneth aside by the flocks of thy companions'?
options: She desires to be where her beloved is, not wandering aimlessly among others
She wants to avoid the company of others completely
She is indifferent about the beloved’s location
She wishes to lead the companions’ flocks
questions.correctAnswer: She desires to be where her beloved is, not wandering aimlessly among others
questions.explanation: In verse 7, the speaker questions why she should be like one who turns aside among others’ flocks, expressing a longing to be with her beloved rather than distracted or misplaced.

questions.question: True or False: Song of Solomon 1:8 encourages the fairest among women to seek guidance by following the flock’s footsteps and feeding beside shepherds’ tents if she does not know where her beloved feeds.
questions.explanation: Verse 8 clearly states, 'If thou know not... go thy way forth by the footsteps of the flock, and feed thy kids beside the shepherds’ tents,' teaching reliance on guidance and fellowship.

questions.question: True or False: Song of Solomon 1:12 implies that the fragrance of spikenard is only noticeable when the king is not present.
questions.explanation: Verse 12 specifically says, 'While the king sitteth at his table, my spikenard sendeth forth the smell thereof,' indicating the fragrance is present during the king’s presence, not absent.

questions.question: True or False: The imagery in Song of Solomon 1:9-10 teaches the importance of recognizing and celebrating the beauty and strength given by God in others.
questions.explanation: Verses 9-10 compare the beloved to horses in Pharaoh's chariots and describe adornments of jewels and gold, illustrating appreciation and celebration of God’s gifts to others.

hard.title: Song of Solomon Chapter 1 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Song of Solomon Chapter 1.

questions.question: According to Song of Solomon 1:13, what is the beloved compared to?
questions.explanation: The beloved is compared to 'a bundle of myrrh' in Song of Solomon 1:13, symbolizing fragrance and intimacy.

questions.question: What is the significance of the 'camphire' mentioned in Song of Solomon 1:14?
options: It symbolizes beauty and fragrance in the vineyards of Engedi
It refers to a type of precious stone
It is a metaphor for strength and courage
It is a name of a city in Solomon's kingdom
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes beauty and fragrance in the vineyards of Engedi
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:14 describes the beloved as 'a cluster of camphire in the vineyards of Engedi,' highlighting beauty and aromatic presence.

questions.question: In Song of Solomon 1:15, what feature is specifically mentioned about the beloved's eyes?
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly states, 'thou hast doves' eyes,' emphasizing gentleness and purity (Song of Solomon 1:15).

questions.question: What does the phrase 'our bed is green' in Song of Solomon 1:16 most likely symbolize?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'our bed is green' metaphorically suggests fertility and renewal, consistent with ancient Near Eastern symbolism (Song of Solomon 1:16).

questions.question: Which materials are mentioned as the beams and rafters of the house in Song of Solomon 1:17?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'The beams of our house are cedar, and our rafters of fir,' indicating durable and precious construction materials (Song of Solomon 1:17).

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Song of Solomon 1:15 with the repetition of 'behold, thou art fair'?
questions.explanation: The repeated phrase 'behold, thou art fair' is an example of parallelism, emphasizing the beloved's beauty (Song of Solomon 1:15).

questions.question: How does the phrase 'he shall lie all night betwixt my breasts' in Song of Solomon 1:13 relate to Old Testament imagery of intimacy?
options: It echoes the close protective relationship seen in Ruth and Boaz
It references the sanctuary imagery in Exodus
It symbolizes the covenant between David and Jonathan
It refers to the priestly garments in Leviticus
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes the close protective relationship seen in Ruth and Boaz
questions.explanation: The intimacy described in Song 1:13 reflects the protective and close relationship like that of Ruth and Boaz (Ruth 3:9), showing care and closeness.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of love surpassing wine as expressed in Song of Solomon 1:2 and 1:4?
questions.explanation: Ephesians 5:25 discusses Christ's love for the church, paralleling the surpassing love described in Song 1:2 and 1:4.

questions.question: In the cultural context of the ancient Near East, what does the use of 'myrrh' in Song of Solomon 1:13 suggest?
options: It signifies sacredness and preciousness often used in burial and worship
It indicates a common food staple
It denotes a type of armor
It represents a form of currency
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies sacredness and preciousness often used in burial and worship
questions.explanation: Myrrh was a costly perfume used in burial and sacred rituals, symbolizing preciousness and sanctity (Song of Solomon 1:13).

questions.question: What Hebrew word translated as 'beloved' in Song of Solomon 1:13 and 1:14 carries the meaning of 'friend' or 'lover'?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Dod' means beloved, friend, or lover, emphasizing intimate affection (Song of Solomon 1:13-14).

questions.question: True or False: Song of Solomon 1:16 declares that the beloved is both fair and pleasant, and also mentions that their bed is green.
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:16 states, 'Behold, thou art fair, my beloved, yea, pleasant: also our bed is green,' confirming the description.

questions.question: True or False: According to Song of Solomon 1:17, the rafters of the house are made of oak and the beams are of pine.
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1:17 specifies the beams are cedar and the rafters are fir, not oak and pine.

questions.question: Which Old Testament location mentioned in Song of Solomon 1:14 is known for its lush vineyards and natural beauty?
questions.explanation: Engedi is noted in Song of Solomon 1:14 as the place of the vineyards, a symbol of natural beauty and fertility.

questions.question: What is the significance of cedar as used in Song of Solomon 1:17 in biblical symbolism?
options: It symbolizes strength, durability, and holiness
It is a common material for temporary shelters
It is associated with foreign idols
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes strength, durability, and holiness
questions.explanation: Cedar wood, as in Song 1:17, symbolizes strength and holiness, often used in the temple and royal buildings (1 Kings 6:9).

questions.question: What cross-biblical theme related to love and marriage is developed in Song of Solomon Chapter 1 and also reflected in Ephesians 5?
options: The mutual love and sacrificial relationship between husband and wife
The laws concerning divorce and remarriage
questions.correctAnswer: The mutual love and sacrificial relationship between husband and wife
questions.explanation: Song of Solomon 1 emphasizes romantic and mutual love, a theme Paul develops in Ephesians 5:22-33 about Christ and the church.

theological.title: Song of Solomon Chapter 1 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Song of Solomon Chapter 1 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the primary theme of the Song of Solomon as introduced in the first verse?
questions.explanation: The opening verse states, 'The song of songs, which is Solomon's' (Song of Solomon 1:1), indicating that it is a love song, distinct in its poetic expression of romantic love.

questions.question: In Song of Solomon 1:2, what is said to be better than wine?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'for thy love is better than wine' (Song of Solomon 1:2), highlighting the value and sweetness of love.

questions.question: What does the speaker compare their beloved's name to in Song of Solomon 1:3?
questions.explanation: The verse describes the beloved's name as 'as ointment poured forth' (Song of Solomon 1:3), indicating its preciousness and sweetness.

questions.question: What imagery is used to describe the beloved in Song of Solomon 1:9?
options: A company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots
questions.correctAnswer: A company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots
questions.explanation: The beloved is compared to 'a company of horses in Pharaoh's chariots' (Song of Solomon 1:9), symbolizing beauty and strength.

questions.question: What does Song of Solomon 1:6 reveal about the speaker's feelings towards their appearance?
questions.explanation: The speaker states, 'I am black, but comely,' indicating a sense of shame regarding their appearance due to external circumstances (Song of Solomon 1:5-6).

questions.question: What is the significance of the imagery of vineyards in Song of Solomon 1:6?
options: It symbolizes neglect and lost potential
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes neglect and lost potential
questions.explanation: The speaker laments that they have not kept their own vineyard, illustrating a neglect of personal beauty or care (Song of Solomon 1:6).

questions.question: In Song of Solomon 1:12, what does the spikenard symbolize?
questions.explanation: The spikenard sending forth its smell while the king sits at his table symbolizes the fragrant and delightful nature of love (Song of Solomon 1:12).

questions.question: What connection does Song of Solomon 1:15 make about the beloved's beauty?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'thou hast doves' eyes' (Song of Solomon 1:15) symbolizes purity and innocence, suggesting the beloved's beauty is profound.

questions.question: How does Song of Solomon 1:4 describe the communal response to love?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Draw me, we will run after thee,' indicating a joyful and enthusiastic response to love (Song of Solomon 1:4).

questions.question: What does the phrase 'our bed is green' in Song of Solomon 1:16 suggest about the relationship?
questions.explanation: The mention of 'our bed is green' (Song of Solomon 1:16) conveys freshness and vitality in the relationship, indicative of flourishing love.

questions.question: What does Song of Solomon 1:17 reveal about the structure of the beloved’s dwelling?
questions.explanation: The verse describes the beams as 'cedar' and rafters as 'fir,' which symbolize strength and durability (Song of Solomon 1:17).

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 5-6 convey about personal identity?
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 illustrate the struggle between external appearance and internal identity, emphasizing that neglect of one's self can lead to feelings of shame.

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated through the beloved's beauty in Song of Solomon 1:10-11?
questions.explanation: The descriptions of beauty and adornment in verses 10-11 reflect the depth and richness of love, illustrating God's desire for beauty in relationships (Song of Solomon 1:10-11).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that the Song of Solomon lacks theological significance. What does Song of Solomon 1:2-3 actually teach?
options: Love is a metaphor for God's relationship with His people
questions.correctAnswer: Love is a metaphor for God's relationship with His people
questions.explanation: The intimate expressions of love in these verses can be viewed as a metaphor for the deep, covenantal love God has for His people, affirming its theological significance (Song of Solomon 1:2-3).

questions.question: How do verses 4 and 7 collectively illustrate the communal aspect of love?
questions.explanation: Verses 4 and 7 emphasize the joy and pursuit of love, indicating that true love is communal and invites others into the experience (Song of Solomon 1:4, 7).
